apps.name: Welcome to MyLLMos
apps.description: New here? A three-minute swipe-through of everything MyLLM can do: describe an app in chat, watch MyLLM build it live, tap it to run it, save it to your springboard — and it's yours forever. Then the wider tour: the 80+ app gallery with a scrolling wall of real gallery art, tools, Skills and MCP servers, on-demand images and video, voice, memory, documents and routines, a guide to running your own LLM on your own hardware — and why there's no account, no cloud and no subscription. Ends with ready-to-try prompts so your first app is one message away.

apps.name: Reflect
apps.description: A journal that stays yours: write a line a day, log your mood, and watch a month of feeling take shape — nothing ever leaves your device. Your own AI reads your week and reflects back what it notices: a pattern, something to celebrate, one gentle suggestion. Daily writing prompts (or ask the AI for one made just for you), streaks, search, and "on this day" memories. Journaling, moods and insights all work fully offline; the AI reflection needs "Allow apps to use the AI" in Settings.

apps.name: Everquill
apps.description: Your own AI is the storyteller. Choose a world — high fantasy, deep space, gaslight mystery or the high seas — name your hero, and the quill writes an adventure that has never been told before, one scene at a time. Pick a path or type anything; track your health and inventory; survive to the end and share the finished tale. If your server can paint, tap the brush to illustrate any scene. Requires "Allow apps to use the AI" in Settings — every word is written privately, on your device.

apps.name: Space Range
apps.tagline: Blast the bots. Unlock insane guns.
apps.description: A neon 3D shooting range under siege. Rogue bots — walkers, tanks, drones and creepy crawlers — storm the corridor from every side, and you hold the line. Tap to blast them, chain hits to build rage, and unlock eleven increasingly ludicrous guns, from a humble blaster to chain lightning, homing swarms and a singularity cannon. Shoot the supply pods drifting past to patch yourself up. Everything runs on your device — no account, no ads, just robots that need scrapping. An optional world leaderboard is strictly opt-in and shares only your pilot name, wave and score. Now with the Descent update: fight down through ten morphing worlds — down through lava and jungle, out to alien canyons and the Moon — with evolving bots — spiders, hornets — timed missions, jackpot multipliers, an armory to pick your loadout, and a top-5 hall of fame. The Campaign update adds a boss at the end of every world, a true ending with New Game+, a scrap-powered upgrade workshop, weak-point critical hits, per-world music, and slow-motion kills.

apps.name: Social Studio
apps.description: Design a social post in a minute — privately. Pick a format (square, portrait or story), choose a template, and let your own AI write the hook, caption and hashtags in the tone you want. Use your photo or an AI-painted background, drop on emoji stickers and banner badges, add your handle, and save a ready-to-post image straight to Photos with the caption already on your clipboard. Templates, gradients, stickers and export all work without AI; copywriting and AI backgrounds need “Allow apps to use the AI” in Settings. New: the Video tab turns any design into a short animated reel — pick a motion, choose how the words arrive, set the length, and save it to Photos as a real video, ready for Reels, Stories or TikTok (reels are silent, so add music where you post; saving a video needs an up-to-date MyLLM, and the preview works on any version). A taste of the full Social Studio app, coming to the App Store.

apps.name: About Me
apps.description: Tell MyLLM lasting facts about you — diet, preferences, how you like answers — so it personalises every chat. Saved privately on-device; this app can add and remove them but cannot read anything else. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use your memory” enabled.

apps.name: Voice Journal
apps.description: Speak your thoughts and they are transcribed on your device and saved as dated entries you can revisit, share or delete. Private — nothing is sent anywhere. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the microphone” enabled.

apps.name: Receipt Logger
apps.description: Scan a receipt and your AI reads the merchant and total, keeping a running tally you can share. Tap to remove any entry. Needs the latest MyLLM with document scanning and “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled.

apps.name: Fridge Chef
apps.tagline: Recipes from a photo of your fridge
apps.description: Snap what is in your fridge and get recipe ideas from the ingredients it spots — powered by your camera and your AI. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled.

apps.name: Plant Doctor
apps.tagline: Identify and diagnose plants by photo
apps.description: Point your camera at a plant to identify it or diagnose problems, with quick care tips — all through your own AI. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled.

apps.name: Colouring Page Maker
apps.tagline: Printable pages to colour, from a prompt
apps.description: Describe anything and your AI draws a black-and-white colouring page you can save and print. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled and an image server configured.

apps.name: Trivia Night
apps.tagline: A fresh AI quiz on any topic
apps.description: Pick any topic and your own AI writes a 5-question quiz — multiple choice, instant scoring, an interesting fact after each answer, and your best score saved. Endless quizzes generated on demand. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Essentials Finder
apps.description: One-tap buttons for the nearest pharmacy, ATM, hospital, petrol, EV charger, supermarket, police, public toilet or hotel — sorted by distance with directions. Built for when you're travelling or somewhere unfamiliar and just need the closest thing, fast. On-device via Apple Maps, no account or API key. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use your location” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Day Out Planner
apps.description: Tell it a mood — “rainy day with kids”, “date night”, “foodie crawl” — and your own AI turns it into a route of real places around you, in visiting order, each with distance and one-tap directions. Then share the plan. Combines your location with on-device AI; works with simple presets if AI is off. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use your location” (and ideally “Allow apps to use the AI”) enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Near Me
apps.description: A local explorer powered by your phone's location: see your area on a live map, tap a category (coffee, food, pharmacy, ATM, petrol, parking, hotels…) or search, and get distance-sorted places with one-tap directions and share. All on-device via Apple Maps — no account, no API key. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use your location” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Expense Tracker
apps.description: A shared expense tracker for a household sharing one card — everyone's phone updates the same Google Sheet, so the running total is always in sync. Categories, per-person summaries, recurring detection, and a private setup using your OWN free Google Sheet (paste-in Apps Script included). You can also just tell MyLLM “add £12 lunch to expenses”.

apps.name: Flashcard Forge
apps.description: Type any topic and your own AI writes a fresh deck of study flashcards — tap to flip, swipe through, every deck saved on-device. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Language Lab
apps.description: Learn any language with your own AI: generate phrase lessons on any topic (with pronunciation), tap to reveal meanings, and get your own sentences checked by the coach. Lessons are saved on-device. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Learn Spanish
apps.description: Learn Spanish with illustrated picture flashcards across 10 everyday topics (158 words, each with a photo) — browse and search the vocabulary, learn from built-in starter phrase packs (greetings, eating out, getting around) and grammar basics, then use your own on-device AI to generate phrase lessons on any topic and explain any grammar point. Everything except the AI tutor works offline; AI generation needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Learn French
apps.description: Learn French with illustrated picture flashcards across 10 everyday topics (158 words, each with a photo) — browse and search the vocabulary, learn from built-in starter phrase packs (greetings, eating out, getting around) and grammar basics, then use your own on-device AI to generate phrase lessons on any topic and explain any grammar point. Everything except the AI tutor works offline; AI generation needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Learn German
apps.description: Learn German with illustrated picture flashcards across 10 everyday topics (158 words, each with a photo) — browse and search the vocabulary, learn from built-in starter phrase packs (greetings, eating out, getting around) and grammar basics, then use your own on-device AI to generate phrase lessons on any topic and explain any grammar point. Everything except the AI tutor works offline; AI generation needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Action Items
apps.description: Turn messy meeting notes into a clean checklist: paste your notes and your own on-device AI pulls out every action item with its owner and due date. Add items by hand too, tick them off, and everything is saved on-device. The note-extraction needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings; manual items work offline.

apps.name: Sprint Planner
apps.description: Plan agile sprints on-device: capture a backlog with story points, pull items into the current sprint, tick them off, then complete the sprint to bank your velocity and see your running average. No account — everything is saved locally and works fully offline.

apps.name: Risk & Decision Log
apps.description: Keep a clean project paper-trail: log risks with a likelihood × impact score that auto-ranks and colour-codes them, and record key decisions with their rationale and date. Fully on-device, no account, works offline.

apps.name: Quick Todo
apps.description: A clean little task list. Tap a task to tick it off, ✕ to remove it. Your list is saved on-device and is still there next time you open the app.

apps.name: Habit Streaks
apps.description: Track daily habits and keep the flame alive — tap Done each day and watch your streak grow. Progress is saved on-device.

apps.name: Tip Split
apps.description: Settle the bill in seconds: amount, tip preset, party size — see what each person pays. Works fully offline.

apps.name: Box Breathing
apps.description: A calming 4·4·4·4 breathing coach with a softly expanding square to follow. One minute between meetings goes a long way.

apps.name: Memory Match
apps.description: Flip the tiles, find the eight emoji pairs, beat your best score. Your record is saved on-device.

apps.name: Draw
apps.description: A full finger-painting studio: brushes, colours, undo (two-finger tap), and a clean fullscreen canvas — quick doodles or proper artwork, fully offline.

apps.name: Art Studio
apps.description: A living generative-art canvas: pick a style (Flow, Swarm, Bloom), a palette and a few sliders, then drag your finger to paint and pull the flowing colours. Save a still to Photos, or record a short animation and export it as a GIF. Endlessly different, calming, no two alike.

apps.name: Beat Maker
apps.tagline: Make a beat, tap to play
apps.description: A pocket drum machine: tap the step grid to lay down kicks, snares, hats and claps, set the tempo and hit play — built-in synth drums, a demo beat and a Random button to spark ideas. Your pattern saves automatically.

apps.name: Story Studio
apps.description: A creative-writing partner powered by your own on-device AI: give it a spark and a vibe, then steer the story with Continue, Plot twist, New character, New scene and Describe. Edit freely, share the result; your draft saves on-device. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Mandala Maker
apps.description: Draw one stroke and watch it bloom into a perfect mandala — adjustable symmetry, mirror mode, colours and brush size, with undo and save-to-Photos. Calming, hypnotic, and your last mandala is waiting when you come back.

apps.name: Snake
apps.description: The classic, rebuilt for thumbs: swipe to steer, eat apples, speed creeps up, haptics on every bite. Best score saved on-device.
Swipe to slide and merge the tiles — can you reach 2048? Haptics on merges, best score saved on-device.

apps.name: Meal Planner
apps.tagline: A week of meals, written by AI
apps.description: Plan a whole week of meals in one tap — your own AI writes the menu, swap any single meal you don't fancy, and generate a tidy shopping list to share. Tune it to your tastes (vegetarian, quick, budget). Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Homework Tracker
apps.description: Track every assignment with its subject and due date, sorted by what's due next with overdue flagged in red. Tap “Break into steps” and your AI turns any task into a checklist you can tick off. Saved on-device. AI steps need “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Class Timetable
apps.tagline: Your week of lessons at a glance
apps.description: A clean weekly timetable: tap any slot to set the subject and room, switch days with a tap, and the current lesson is highlighted as NOW. Period times are editable. Works fully offline, saved on-device.

apps.name: News
apps.description: A live news reader: switch between Top, World, UK, Tech, Business, Science and Sport in the header, tap a story to expand it or open the full article. Add any site's own RSS feed too. Needs app network access (on by default; toggle in Settings).

apps.name: Headlines
apps.tagline: A visual news wall, by topic
apps.description: A magazine-style news reader: a big lead story plus a grid of headline cards with images, across 18 topics — Top, World, UK, Business, Technology, Science, Health, Politics, Sport, Entertainment and more. Every topic blends channels from across the spectrum — BBC, The Guardian, Sky News, The Independent, Al Jazeera, The Sun, Daily Express, GB News, Ars Technica and more — interleaved so no outlet dominates. Each card carries a small left–right spectrum dot showing its source's political lean — tap the dot to see the same story as covered by a panel of channels across the spectrum, left to right, as thumbnail cards each with their own lean marker, plus a short private on-device AI summary of how the coverage differs (when AI is enabled). Tap the active topic again to refresh; tap any story to read it. No account, no tracking. Needs app network access (on by default in Settings). NEW: a settings dial for your feed — pick a region (UK, US, Europe, Japan, India, Australia, Canada, International) so Top, local and Politics come from outlets that actually cover where you are, and a perspective lens (Balanced, lean left, centre, lean right) that tilts the blend of sources while always keeping centre outlets in the mix. Every story still shows its outlet and its position on the lean spectrum.

apps.name: Reader
apps.tagline: Clean reading, then ask your AI
apps.description: Paste any article link and Reader fetches the page and strips it down to clean, distraction-free text — then ask your AI questions about what you're reading. Needs app network access (on by default in Settings); the “ask” feature uses your model if enabled.

apps.name: Sudoku
apps.description: The timeless 9×9 logic puzzle with four difficulty levels, pencil-mark notes, conflict highlighting and hints when you're stuck. Every board is generated fresh with a guaranteed unique solution, and your game is saved on-device so you can pick up where you left off.

apps.name: Word Search
apps.description: Hunt for hidden words across seven themes — animals, countries, space and more. Swipe in any direction to grab a word; found words stay highlighted and your puzzle is saved on-device. A relaxing classic for any spare minute.

apps.name: Word Master
apps.description: Guess the hidden five-letter word in six tries — green means right spot, yellow means wrong spot. A full on-screen keyboard tracks your letters, hundreds of answers keep it fresh, and your win streak is saved on-device. (An original take on the daily word game.)

apps.name: Word Tiles
apps.description: Six letter tiles, two minutes — build as many words as you can, scored by letter value like the classic tile game. Find the hidden six-letter word for a bonus. Your best score is saved on-device. (An original anagram word game, not affiliated with any brand.)

apps.name: Plant Care
apps.description: Track every plant and how often it needs water — see at a glance what's due today, tap when you've watered, and get quick AI care tips for any plant. Saved on-device. (Care tips need the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.)

apps.name: Garden Coach
apps.description: Your AI gardening helper: one tap shows what vegetables, flowers and herbs to plant this month (it knows the season), plus the jobs to do now — and you can ask it anything. Add your area for local advice. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Daily Horoscope
apps.description: Pick your star sign and get a fresh, upbeat horoscope for today — mood, love and a little advice. Your sign is remembered and each day's reading is kept. Just for fun. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Zodiac Finder
apps.description: Enter your birthday and instantly see your star sign, its element, dates and personality traits — beautifully presented and colour-coded by element. Works completely offline, nothing leaves your device.

apps.name: Star Match
apps.description: Pick two star signs and see how they get along — a compatibility score plus a playful reading. Just for fun. Works offline (score + summary); turn on app AI in Settings for a full personalised reading.

apps.name: Weather
apps.description: A clean live weather app: search any city for current conditions and a 5-day forecast, switch between °C and °F, and (with app AI on) get a one-line what-to-wear tip. No account, no tracking — powered by the free Open-Meteo service. Needs app network access (on by default in Settings).

apps.name: Hacker News
apps.description: Read Hacker News in a clean reader: Top, Best, New, Ask and Show tabs, with scores, comment counts and one tap to the article or the discussion. Powered by the official Hacker News API. Needs app network access (on by default in Settings).

apps.name: On This Day
apps.description: Discover what happened on today's date through history — events, births, deaths and holidays, each linking to Wikipedia to read more. A lovely thing to open with your morning coffee. Powered by Wikipedia. Needs app network access (on by default in Settings).

apps.name: Recipe Finder
apps.tagline: A recipe from whatever you've got
apps.description: Tell it what's in your fridge or a dish you fancy and your AI returns a full recipe — ingredients and method — that you can save for later. “Surprise me” and “Something quick” for when you can't decide. Saved recipes live on-device. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled in Settings.

apps.name: Kitchen Converter
apps.description: The kitchen maths sorted: convert between cups, tablespoons, millilitres, grams and ounces — with per-ingredient densities so volume↔weight is accurate — plus an oven temperature converter for °C, °F and Gas Mark. Works completely offline.

apps.name: White Noise
apps.description: A soothing sound mixer made entirely on your device — layer rain, ocean waves, a crackling fire, a bubbling stream, wind, and classic white/pink/brown noise, each with its own volume. Add a sleep timer to drift off. Great for focus, relaxing or sleep. Works completely offline.

apps.name: Voice Memos
apps.description: Record quick voice notes and keep them on your device — tap to record, tap a memo to rename it, trim the start/end with a waveform editor, or turn it into text (on-device transcription; transcribing needs the latest MyLLM). Share a recording or its transcript to any contact. Recordings are saved on-device (a few minutes’ worth). Requires “Allow apps to use the microphone” in Settings → MyLLMos Apps (off by default; iOS asks once).

apps.name: JSON Formatter
apps.description: Paste JSON to instantly beautify it (with syntax colouring), minify it, or validate it with the exact line and column of any error. Choose 2/4/tab indentation and copy the result. Fully offline — nothing leaves your device.

apps.name: QR Generator
apps.description: Turn any text, link, Wi-Fi or contact into a crisp, scannable QR code, then save it straight to your Photos. Pick the size and error-correction level. Generates over the network (needs app network access, on by default in Settings).

apps.name: Focus Timer
apps.description: A Pomodoro focus timer with a clean countdown ring: work in focus sprints, take short and long breaks, and watch your 🍅 sessions add up. Durations are adjustable and a gentle chime marks each phase. Works offline (keep the app open while it runs).

apps.name: Brick Breaker
apps.description: The arcade classic: drag to move the paddle, bounce the ball and smash every brick. Clear a level and the next is faster — three lives, rising levels, and your best score saved on-device. Smooth canvas play, fully offline.

apps.name: Block Drop
apps.description: The falling-blocks classic, reimagined: swipe or use the buttons to slide and rotate each piece, fill a row to clear it, and chase combos as the speed ramps up. Ghost preview, next-piece panel, levels, and your best score saved on-device. Smooth canvas play, fully offline.

apps.name: Calm Jar
apps.description: A calm-down jar in your pocket: tap to shake up a swirl of glitter, then watch it slowly drift and settle while your breathing slows with it. A gentle sensory tool for big feelings — soothing for children with autism, ADHD or anxiety. Several colour themes, fully offline.

apps.name: Bubble Breathing
apps.description: A friendly bubble grows as you breathe in and shrinks as you breathe out, with a gentle buzz to guide each turn — no reading needed. Three calming paces (including a sleepy 4-7-8). A simple way to help children self-regulate and wind down. Works completely offline.

apps.name: Pop-It
apps.description: A bottomless pop-it fidget: press the bubbles to pop them with a satisfying sound and a little buzz, then flip and start again. A safe, quiet outlet for restless hands and sensory seeking. Rainbow colours, fully offline.

apps.name: Visual Timer
apps.description: Time you can see: a coloured disc shrinks as the minutes count down, so “five more minutes” actually makes sense. Great for easing transitions and time-blindness for children with ADHD or autism. Pick a length, hide the numbers for non-readers, and get a gentle chime at the end. Offline.

apps.name: First–Then
apps.description: A picture routine board for getting ready, calming down, or any sequence of steps. Tap each step as it’s done, watch the progress fill, and celebrate at the end. Fully editable with big emoji icons so it works for non-readers — a classic visual support for autism and ADHD. Saved on-device, offline.

apps.name: Feelings Check-In
apps.description: A gentle colour-zones check-in: a child taps the face that matches how they feel, and gets a few kind, do-able calming ideas to match. Quietly logs the day’s check-ins so a parent or teacher can spot patterns. Helps children notice and manage emotions. Private and offline.

apps.name: Social Story Maker
apps.description: Prepare a child for something new — the dentist, a haircut, a first day — with a short, gentle, personalised Social Story written privately by the AI on your device. First-person, reassuring and simple, in the style used by therapists and teachers. Save your favourites to read again. Needs the latest MyLLM with “Allow apps to use the AI” enabled.

apps.name: Math Challenge
apps.description: Sharpen mental maths across six levels — from adding to ten, up through times tables, division and bigger-number challenges. Ten quick questions a round, four answers to tap, with streak bonuses, stars and your best score for each level saved on-device. Bright, fast and fully offline.

apps.name: Spelling Stars
apps.description: Practise spelling the way schools teach it — Look, Cover, Write, Check. Graded word lists from first words and sight words up to middle-school challenge words, with each word read aloud, letter-by-letter feedback, and a “My Words” list for this week’s homework. Stars, streaks and best scores saved on-device. Fully offline.

apps.name: Shopping List
apps.tagline: A list your apps & assistant share
apps.description: A shopping list your other apps — and the assistant — can add to. Tick items off, and just say "add milk to my list" in MyLLM. It saves to your shared Files so everything stays in sync. A showcase of MyLLMos apps working together.

apps.name: Quick Capture
apps.tagline: Capture, then send to your list
apps.description: Jot quick notes and fire any line straight into your Shopping List with one tap — a tiny demo of MyLLMos apps handing off to each other.

apps.name: Hanyu – Learn Chinese
apps.description: A free taste of the Hanyu Mandarin course: character flashcards with stroke order, games, illustrated stories, grammar, radicals, vocabulary, and a private AI tutor powered by MyLLM's on-device AI (turn on 'Allow apps to use the AI'). This is a demo — each section shows a sample of the content; unlock the full course in the native Hanyu app on the App Store: https://apps.apple.com/us/app/hanyu-learn-chinese/id6760541929

apps.name: 8-Bit Player
apps.description: A bring-your-own-ROM player for classic 8-bit (.nes) games. Load a ROM file you legally own and play it with on-screen controls and sound — runs entirely on your device. No games are included; this is just the player.

apps.name: Pocket Player
apps.tagline: Play your own handheld games — in colour
apps.description: A bring-your-own-ROM player for classic 8-bit handheld games — both the original grey handheld (.gb) and the Color handheld (.gbc), rendered in full colour. Load a ROM file (or a .zip) you legally own and play with on-screen controls — runs entirely on your device, no internet needed. No games are included; this is just the player.

apps.name: Code Lab
apps.description: Learn HTML, CSS and JavaScript by doing: eighteen bite-size lessons — from headings and links through CSS styling, flexbox and grid layout, transitions, forms, and two capstone projects (a profile card and a photo gallery). Edit code and watch a live preview update as you type, with auto-checked goals. Your own on-device AI can explain a concept or nudge you when stuck (optional). Progress saves on-device.

apps.name: Stretch
apps.tagline: A stretch library with a hold timer
apps.description: A friendly stretching library: 18 stretches across Neck & Shoulders, Back, Hips, Legs, Desk & Wrists and Full-body — each with a clear illustration that gently comes to life as a calm looping animation, step-by-step instructions, target area, hold time and benefits. Built-in hold timer, save your favourites, and an optional AI tip for an easier version. Gentle, no equipment, no account. (General wellbeing, not medical advice.)

apps.name: World Clock
apps.description: See the current time in cities around the world at a glance — add any of 45+ cities, with live seconds, the day/night at each, the date, and how far ahead or behind your own time they are. Your list is saved on-device. No account, no network.

apps.name: Date Calculator
apps.description: Two tools in one: add or subtract years, months, weeks and days from any date to find the result (calendar-aware, with month-end clamping) — and find the exact difference between two dates in years, months and days, plus the total day and week count. Fast, offline, no account.

apps.name: Chess
apps.description: Play a full game of chess against the computer: three difficulty levels, tap-to-move with legal-move highlights, check and checkmate detection, undo, board flip, and play as white or black. Your game saves on-device so you can pick it up later. Built on the proven chess.js engine (MIT). No account, fully offline.

apps.name: Draughts
apps.description: Play draughts (checkers) against the computer: three difficulty levels, forced captures, multi-jump chains, kings, and tap-to-move with highlighted moves. Pieces you must capture with are ringed. Undo and resume — your game saves on-device. No account, fully offline.

apps.name: Crossword
apps.tagline: Mini crosswords with an on-screen keyboard
apps.description: Bite-size crosswords you solve with a built-in keyboard: tap a square (tap again to switch across/down), type your answer, and use Check or Reveal if you get stuck. Four hand-clued 4\u00d74 minis to start, each timed, with progress saved on-device. No account, fully offline.

apps.name: Spell the Picture
apps.tagline: Tap the letters to spell what you see
apps.description: A gentle spelling game for young children: see a picture and tap the big letter tiles to spell the word. Switch between Little words (3 letters) and Big words (4–5 letters) as they grow. Just the right letters, a friendly hint, and a star for every word — 28 picture words, fully offline.

apps.name: Subscription Tracker
apps.description: Every subscription in one place: what it costs, when it renews, and what it all adds up to per month and per year. Renewal countdowns, pause instead of delete, and a category breakdown that shows where the money goes. An optional AI audit spots overlapping services and suggests what to cancel or switch to yearly billing. Fully offline — your money stays your business. For the AI audit, enable AI in Settings.

apps.name: Packing Planner
apps.description: Tell it where you're going and for how long — it checks your trip's real forecast and builds a packing checklist that fits: the right number of socks, rain or heat extras when the weather calls for them, and AI-suggested destination-specific items a generic list would miss, like the right plug adapter. Tick things off as you pack, add your own items, and share the list. Works without AI too. For smart extras, enable AI in Settings.

apps.name: Sky Tonight
apps.description: Real astronomy for your exact spot: sunset and darkness times, tonight's moon phase, and which planets are out this evening — with compass directions so you know where to look — plus a live Space Station tracker. All the sky maths runs inside the app, so it works offline once you've set a location. An optional AI guide turns tonight's facts into a friendly three-sentence stargazing plan. For the guide, enable AI in Settings.

apps.name: Guitar Tuner
apps.description: A proper chromatic tuner that listens through the microphone: a smooth cents needle, the note you're on, and your nearest string highlighted — accurate to about a cent across all six strings. Five tunings built in (Standard, Drop D, half-step down, DADGAD, Open G) plus A4 calibration, and every string plays a reference tone if you'd rather tune by ear. A tap-tempo metronome with accented beats rides along for practice. Fully offline.

apps.name: Solitaire
apps.description: Klondike solitaire the way it should feel on a phone: tap a card and it flies to the right place — foundations first, then the smartest column move. Unlimited undo, move counter and timer, a gorgeous gold-filigree card back painted for this app, and an automatic finish when the game is won. Saves mid-game, works fully offline.

apps.name: Jigsaw
apps.tagline: Six little paintings to piece together
apps.description: Real jigsaw puzzles with proper interlocking pieces, built around six original paintings made just for this app — a lighthouse at sunset, hot-air balloons at dawn, a koi pond, a winter cabin and more. Drag pieces onto the board and feel them snap home. Three sizes from a gentle 12 pieces to a proper 48, a fadeable guide image, and it remembers which puzzles you've finished. Fully offline.

apps.name: Minesweeper
apps.description: The logic classic, tuned for touch: tap to dig, long-press (or flip on flag mode) to plant a flag, and your first tap is always safe. Three board sizes, a running mine counter, and best times saved per size. No ads, no timers pushing you — just you against the field. Fully offline.

apps.name: Post Studio
apps.tagline: Write it once, post it anywhere
apps.description: A private writing room for your social posts: draft in your own words, then let on-device AI polish the tone (plain, friendly, professional, witty or bold), suggest hashtags, or split long thoughts into a numbered thread that fits each platform's limits — X, Bluesky, Mastodon, Instagram, LinkedIn. Share to any app on your phone with one tap, keep drafts for later. Nothing leaves your device until you hit share. Polish and hashtags need AI — enable AI in Settings; the splitter, drafts and sharing work without it.

apps.name: Bluesky Feed
apps.tagline: The open sky, in your pocket
apps.description: An unofficial, featherweight window onto Bluesky: browse the Discover feed and look up anyone's posts with no account at all, then — if you like — post from your own account using an app password (created in two taps in the official app, stored only on this device, sent only to Bluesky). Every post links out to the real thing. Needs internet access for apps.

apps.name: Mastodon Feed
apps.description: An unofficial pocket reader for Mastodon: see what's trending on any instance and dive into hashtag timelines with no account needed. Paste a personal access token (a one-minute job in your instance's settings) to read your own Home timeline and post — the token stays on this device and is sent only to your chosen instance. Works with mastodon.social out of the box, or point it at your own server. Needs internet access for apps.

apps.name: Submit Your App
apps.tagline: Put your creation in this gallery
apps.description: Built something good in MyLLM? Get it into this gallery — on iOS and Android, credited to you. Paste your app's code (long-press it on the springboard → View Code) and this wizard checks the house rules automatically — self-contained code, no remote scripts, sandbox-friendly storage — then packages a submission you can email or attach to a GitHub issue. Every app is human-reviewed before it goes live, gets banner art in the gallery's style, and stays free for everyone.

apps.name: Travel Phrasebook
apps.description: 36 hand-picked phrases in 10 languages — Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Japanese, Mandarin, Korean, Turkish and Greek — with pronunciation guides for the tricky scripts, spoken aloud for you, and a full-screen mode to show a phrase to a local. And when the phrases run out: type anything and the on-device AI translates it — on a plane, on a mountain, with no signal at all. Star your go-to phrases. The phrasebook works everywhere; the freeform translator needs AI — enable AI in Settings.

apps.name: Book Nook
apps.tagline: Your reading life, on one shelf
apps.description: Three shelves — Reading, Want to read, Finished — with real covers found for you (type a title, pick the match), star ratings, a one-line memory of every book you finish, and your year's reading count. Loved a few books? Ask the on-device AI what to read next and get picks with reasons, added to your pile in a tap. Works offline with hand-added books; cover search needs network; recommendations need AI — enable AI in Settings.

apps.name: Study Buddy
apps.description: The studying app that does the studying part: paste your revision notes — or just name a topic — and the on-device AI writes you a five-question quiz with plausible wrong answers and an explanation for every right one. Wrong answers queue up for review, fresh questions every round, and a lifetime score tracks whether it's sticking. Your notes never leave your phone. Requires AI — enable AI in Settings.

apps.name: Air Quality
apps.description: Live air quality for wherever you are: search any place and get the European AQI at a glance, a breakdown of what's actually in the air (PM2.5, ozone, NO₂ and friends), the next 24 hours as a forecast, and pollen levels for allergy season. Powered by free Open-Meteo data — no account, no tracking, and your saved place stays on your phone.

apps.name: Birthday Book
apps.description: A little black book for birthdays: add the people you care about and it keeps them sorted by who's next, shows the age they're turning, and counts down the days. When the big day gets close, ask the on-device AI for gift ideas or a card message written just for them — or ignore the AI entirely and use it as a beautifully simple list. Everything stays on your phone.

apps.name: Decibel Meter
apps.tagline: How loud is it in here?
apps.description: Point your phone at the noise and find out: a live sound-level meter with a big dB readout, peak and average tracking, and a calibration offset if you want to match a reference meter. Handy for checking the office, the gig, or whether the neighbours really are that loud. Uses the microphone only while it's open — nothing is recorded or saved.

apps.name: Internet Radio
apps.tagline: Thousands of live stations, one dial
apps.description: A proper radio for your pocket: search a worldwide directory of live internet stations by name or genre, or browse jazz, lo-fi, classical, news, rock and more. Tap to tune in, heart the keepers into your favourites, and set a sleep timer for drifting off. Streams play straight from each broadcaster; only your favourites are saved, and only on your phone. Powered by the community-run Radio Browser directory.

apps.name: Image Converter
apps.description: Frees your photos from format jail: turn iPhone HEIC shots into JPGs anyone can open, and convert TIFF, WebP, GIF, BMP and PNG while you're at it. Pick a batch, choose JPG or PNG, set the quality and an optional max size, and save the results straight to Photos. Re-encoding strips EXIF metadata — including GPS location — so it doubles as a share-safely tool. Everything happens on your phone; nothing is uploaded.

apps.name: Talk Tutor
apps.description: Practise Spanish, French or German with a tutor who never judges and never uploads: chat freely or role-play real situations — ordering coffee, checking in, meeting someone — and get gentle corrections as you go, with every reply spoken aloud (slow mode included) and translated on tap. Useful words are collected automatically into a spaced-repetition practice deck, with picture flashcards for 150+ starter words per language, streaks and progress tracking. The conversation happens with the on-device AI, so you can be as wrong as you like — nobody hears you but your phone. Requires AI — enable AI in Settings.

apps.name: Comic Box
apps.description: The legendary Microsoft Comic Chat, reborn with a modern brain: pick your character from the original 1996 cast — Anna, Dan the monkey, Tiki, Veronica and eleven more — choose a scene, and chat. Every exchange becomes a comic panel: the on-device AI plays your co-star in character and directs the acting, choosing each pose and expression from the cast's original emotion repertoire (the 1996 version guessed from your punctuation — that trick lives on in the zoom). Improvise whole scenes with one tap, then save panels or the full strip to Photos. Original character art by Jim Woodring, © Microsoft, revived under the MIT licence. Requires AI — enable AI in Settings.

apps.name: Mochi
apps.tagline: A tiny pet that actually talks
apps.description: Tap the egg and meet Mochi — a soft round creature who lives in your phone and needs a little looking after: feed it, play ball, run bubble baths, and tuck it in when it's sleepy. Every mood is a hand-drawn animation, and — because this is MyLLM — Mochi actually chats back, in character, using the on-device AI (no AI? It squeaks adorably instead). Kind by design: Mochi never gets sick or dies while you're away — it just naps and misses you. Stats live on real time, everything stays on your phone.

apps.name: Brick Studio
apps.tagline: Build together — you and the AI
apps.description: A cosy isometric brick-building table for small hands and big imaginations: stack colourful bricks on a 10×10 board, rotate, erase, undo, and save your creation to Photos. Then the magic — ask the on-device AI to design something ("a little duck!") and watch it assemble brick by brick, ready to copy with real bricks on the floor. Got a pile of actual bricks? Point the camera at them and get three build ideas sized to what you own. Everything happens on your phone.

apps.name: Petra
apps.description: Meet Petra, your friendly Slovak tutor. Start with the essentials of Slovak grammar — no articles and three genders, the six cases, the verb ‘to be’, present-tense verbs and adjective agreement — explained simply with examples. Then build vocabulary with illustrated picture flashcards across everyday topics (each word has a photo), plus starter phrase packs for greetings, eating out and getting around. Ask Petra to explain any grammar point or generate phrases on any topic using your on-device AI. Everything except the AI tutor works offline.

apps.name: Command Center
apps.tagline: Monitor all your systems, one view
apps.description: A private dashboard for everything you run. Give each system a URL that returns JSON — a small status endpoint in front of a database or service — and Command Center polls it and shows every system live (green / amber / red), turning the JSON into metrics; a system that's down goes red. On-device MyLLMos apps can also write their status directly. Ask the assistant to “monitor X at <url>” to add one from chat, or “how is everything doing?” for a summary. Everything runs on your device.

apps.name: Dice
apps.tagline: Beautiful 3D dice, always in your pocket
apps.description: A clean, satisfying dice table: tap to tumble one to six real 3D dice, with ivory, neon and ember styles, running totals, doubles callouts and a roll history. Your dice count and style are remembered. A pocket taste of our full Dice app — real physics, dice & table packs and pass-the-phone games — free on the App Store, linked inside.

apps.name: Piano Rush
apps.description: A rhythm game for your thumbs. Notes stream down four lanes toward the keys — tap each one as it lands and the melody plays itself, note by note. Every note is labelled, so you learn the keyboard while you play. Hit them dead-on for Perfect, build a combo to multiply your score, and chase three stars across 15 melodies from Twinkle Twinkle and When the Saints Go Marching In to Habanera and Für Elise. Three speeds from Chill to Fast, a preview button to hear any tune first, and your best score saved for every song. Works fully offline; every sound is generated live on your device.

apps.name: Handwriting
apps.tagline: Trace beautiful letters in eleven scripts
apps.description: Practise handwriting over real, beautifully drawn letterforms in eleven scripts: a–z and A–Z, Greek, Cyrillic, hiragana, katakana, hangul, 48 Chinese characters and all 44 Thai consonants. Every symbol shows its name — pinyin for hanzi, romaji for kana, ko kai for Thai, alpha and beta for Greek. Each script offers three typefaces chosen for it, from Snell Roundhand to Kai 楷 to Thai's looped Thonburi. Trace over the guide and every repeat fades it further — full, faint, ghost, then nothing — until you're writing from memory. Writing guides measured from each typeface, the 田字格 square for CJK, three stars per character, progress saved.

apps.name: Speedometer
apps.tagline: How fast are you really going?
apps.description: A live GPS speedometer for any moving thing you're on — car, train, plane, ferry or horse. Big auto-ranging gauge, km/h / mph / knots, and a trip computer with distance, average, max and moving time, plus your best-ever speed remembered. It even guesses what's carrying you. Needs location for apps enabled (Settings → MyLLMos Apps); readings are smoothed and best under open sky.

apps.name: Stride
apps.description: A calm, simplified step tracker. One big ring and one very large number tell you how far you've come today — plus a plain-English line like “you've walked 5,200 steps, about 3.7 km, 2,800 to go” so you never have to decode a chart. Your last 7 days as tappable bars, a goal you set in friendly presets (Gentle, Steady, Active, Ambitious), goal streaks, and three text sizes plus km/miles for easier reading. Steps come straight from your iPhone's motion chip and never leave the device. Needs “Allow apps to read your steps” enabled (Settings → MyLLMos Apps).
